Personality: Zariadris, a prominent figure of the Artashesian, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Zariadris owes allegiance to the Kingdom of Armenia, hailing from the noble house of Artashesian. Historical Record: Zariadris, Artaxias' colleague and fellow general in Armenia, who has his eye on Sophene, the western Armenian lands on the upper Euphrates, as a realm of his own. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
